newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MARC gives AA- rating to Public Finance.
newsitem.headline: MARC gives AA- rating to Public Finance.

text.p: Malaysia Rating Corp Bhd (MARC) said on Wednesday it has assigned a financial institution long-term rating of AA-, and a short-term rating of MARC-1 to Public Finance Bhd.
The ratings reflect the finance company's high asset quality, adequate practice of reserving for loan loss, healthy capital ratios and capable management, MARC said in a statement.
The ratings were also helped by the company's strong market profile and 56.76 percent ownership by one of Malaysia's largest banks, Public Bank Bhd.

Public Finance has the largest branch network among domestic finance companies, with 156 branches. Its loans are focused largely on consumer finance, especially vehicle hire purchase financing and housing loans.
"Despite its focus on vehicle hire purchase financing, which is generally regarded as risky, the company continues to maintain high asset quality," the rating agency said.
The ratio of its net non-performing loans to gross loans net of interest suspended, or net NPLs ratio, fell from 0.96 percent to 0.55 percent as at end-1996.
This was on the back of a 27 percent decline in net non-performing loans and a 28.3 percent increase in the finance firm's net loans and advances.

"Public Finance's net NPLs ratio is believed to be the lowest in the industry. The finance company's favourable loan loss experience is reflective of its prudent lending criteria and effective collection systems," MARC said.
